planets.name: 55 Cnc b
planets.description: Planet of 55 Cnc found by radial velocity, with a 14.7-day year, found in 1996.

radius.source: the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since 55 Cnc b does not transit

mass.source: Moutou et al. (2026), A&A 705, A190, Table 3: minimum mass (m sin i) 276 +/- 9 Earth masses from the star's radial velocities; at the assumed tilt of 93.9 degrees the mass is 0.2% more

orbit.source: Moutou et al. (2026), A&A 705, A190, Table 3, a fit of the star's radial velocities (a/R* is its 0.118 au over the star's recorded 656,045 km); the orbit's plane is assumed, from Xiao et al. (2026, arXiv:2609.01377)
orbit.assumedPlane: Approximate orbital placement. No source measures this planet's tilt or the direction of its orbit on the sky. Both are taken from 55 Cnc d, for which Xiao et al. (2026, arXiv:2609.01377) measure inclination 93.9 (+6.9, -6.7) degrees and ascending node 124 (+28, -30) degrees from radial velocities joined with Hipparcos and Gaia astrometry, on the assumption that the planets share one plane. Across 19 systems that paper finds the tilts of inner and outer planets differ by a Rayleigh scale of 15.8 (+2.8, -2.6) degrees. The period, eccentricity, argument and timing are measured.

text.card: 55 Cnc b was found in 1996 by radial velocity; it does not cross its star.
text.introduction: It is one of 5 planets known around 55 Cnc; its size is a model. Its tilt is not measured: it is drawn in the plane measured for 55 Cnc d.
text.locator: Moutou et al. (2026), A&A 705, A190, Table 3: P 14.651552 d, Tconj 2455495.595, e 0.0029, omega 0.41 rad, a 0.118 au, m sin i 276 Earth masses; Xiao et al. (2026), Table 4, 55 Cnc d: I 93.9 deg, Omega 124 deg (assumed for this planet); NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table: disc_year 1996, sy_pnum 7, 5 of them with hostname 55 Cnc; pscomppars calculated pl_radj 1.24

quotes.title: 55 Cancri Ab
quotes.card: 55 Cancri Ab, formally named Galileo, is an exoplanet orbiting the Sun-like star 55 Cancri A every 14.65 days.
quotes.introduction: It is the second planet in order of distance from its star, and is an example of a hot Jupiter, or possibly rather "warm Jupiter".
